problem_restatement: Quantify how often the three staged v52 routes have historically produced attributable entry signals without converting sparse route studies into a portfolio-frequency or profitability promise.

route_cadence.cadence_assessment: Recent evidence supports approximately 0.6-0.7 entry signals per week, materially below the development period. The forward interval contains one trade and cannot establish a stable rate.
route_cadence.comparability_limit: The artifact's stale exit-reason label says target_2r, but its frozen replay parameter is target_r_multiple=3.0 and matches v52. The historical replay uses 0.25% dynamic risk and 5x leverage rather than v52's 10% margin and 10x cap; entry/exit timing and occupancy remain informative in the observed no-liquidation paths, while dollar PnL is not exact v52 sizing.

route_cadence.v52_exit_contract: 60 bps fixed stop, 60 bps fixed target, 24h fallback
route_cadence.cadence_assessment: The signal mechanism has been comparatively stable near 0.4-0.6 signals per week, but the exact later sample contains one signal.
route_cadence.comparability_limit: The older long-window portfolio studies use 35% margin, 30x leverage, and a 26.67 bps target. They support entry-signal cadence only. The separate taker-parity artifact tests the v52 60 bps target on six development paths and one forward path, not a full exact-v52 portfolio replay.

route_cadence.v52_exit_contract: 80 bps fixed stop, aligned opposite-signal close, 8h soft deadline with frozen regime extension, 24h hard fallback
route_cadence.cadence_assessment: Development produced about one aligned entry per week; the descriptive later window produced one entry in two weeks. The later interval is too sparse to establish a rate.
route_cadence.comparability_limit: The alignment discriminator was specified after subgroup inspection, and the later confirmation window had already been opened. Its cadence and economics remain descriptive rather than untouched confirmation.

portfolio_cadence_diagnostic.planning_interpretation: The current evidence is most consistent with roughly one to two staged entry signals per week, not daily trading. This is a low-confidence planning diagnostic, not a forecast or promotion gate.
why_the_sum_is_not_exact: Both BTC providers share one BTC position and can suppress each other through occupancy.
The Hulk replay matches the 3R barrier but uses a different sizing/leverage contract, so its dollar economics are not exact v52 results.
The HYPE alignment later interval contains one post-selected descriptive trade.
Each single-trade forward rate has an extremely wide exact Poisson interval.
The opened common-window replay contains only three non-overlapping winners, so it measures observed interaction but cannot estimate collision frequency or durable profitability.

current_v51_runtime_observation.interpretation: The current run contains no staged-route entry opportunity. Generic HYPE absence implies no aligned v2 entry in the same interval, but v2 is not the active v51 provider identity.

opened_common_window_portfolio.interpretation: The three exact route lifecycles were positive after route-native modeled costs and an additional seven-bps stress, with no observed BTC collision. This is sparse descriptive evidence, not a profit forecast or proof that the routes are jointly robust.

highest_value_next_investigation.objective: After technical v52 acceptance, collect exact attributable live entries, exits, costs, occupancy decisions, and missed opportunities without changing the frozen route contracts.
minimum_output: at least one resolved HYPE short lifecycle because that configured scope is absent from the common window
every BTC cross-provider collision or occupancy suppression
route and portfolio entries per week with exact observation time
venue fees, funding, slippage, acknowledgement latency, stops, targets, opposite signals, and timer exits
largest-winner sensitivity and exact live return on entry margin
explicit data gaps, rejected orders, stale decisions, and unresolved lifecycle evidence
comparison with the opened common-window planning result without treating it as a forecast
highest_value_next_investigation.success_criterion: Every prospective v52 provider decision reconciles to an entry, close, route conflict, occupancy withholding, technical rejection, or explicit ineligible state, and every completed lifecycle reconciles to venue economics.
highest_value_next_investigation.failure_criterion: Any source mismatch, unexplained order or lifecycle, missing configured scope telemetry, stale decision submission, cost reconciliation failure, or unresolved protection state invalidates the forward window.

recommendation.recommendation: Keep v52 staged through the verified flat cutover, then collect prospective exact-route evidence without loosening the routes merely to manufacture activity.
recommendation.why_now: The opened common-window replay now supports the one-to-two-entry-per-week planning range, but it contains only three winners, no BTC collision, and no HYPE short lifecycle.
recommendation.evidence_reviewed: Frozen Hulk partition and forward artifacts, sweep long-window studies, exact 60/60 taker-parity paths, HYPE alignment replay, staged v52 config, the exact common-window shared-account replay, and fresh v51 drain telemetry.
recommendation.observed_problem_or_opportunity: The exact common window produced three non-overlapping winners and positive stressed net PnL, but the sample is too sparse and directionally incomplete to establish profitability.
recommendation.applicable_market_regime: Provider-specific frozen entry conditions; cadence is expected to vary with volatility, compression, and sweep availability.
recommendation.alternatives_considered: Assume timeframe equals frequency, sum route rates without occupancy, add another asset immediately, relax entry gates, or run the common-window replay.
recommendation.expected_upside: A source-correct prospective baseline for determining whether v52 produces meaningful opportunity and whether an additional diversifying route is actually needed.
recommendation.main_risks_and_failure_modes: Three-trade selection optimism, post-selected HYPE alignment, missing HYPE-short evidence, future BTC occupancy, execution degradation, and treating linearly normalized historical PnL as a forecast.
recommendation.validation_completed: Route-level counts and Garwood intervals were recalculated; the exact common window reconciled all three route lifecycles through one $5K account, exact priority, 10% margin per position, route-native costs, and a seven-bps incremental stress.
recommendation.validation_still_required: Prospective v52 post-start technical acceptance and exact live lifecycle collection, especially HYPE short and any BTC provider collision.
recommendation.success_metrics: Every signal is reconciled, cadence is reported with uncertainty, no hidden technical gaps remain, and after-cost economics are not largest-winner dependent.
recommendation.failure_or_rollback_triggers: A materially lower realized cadence, repeated after-cost losses, persistent occupancy conflicts, friction beyond evidence, or any provider/source identity mismatch.
recommendation.confidence_level: high on arithmetic and source identity; medium on the one-to-two-per-week planning range; low on future profitability because the common window has three winners

falsifier: Replace the planning range or positive descriptive interpretation when prospective v52 evidence produces materially different cadence, route economics, BTC occupancy, HYPE side composition, costs, or unresolved source/execution attribution.
